summary: The retry loop no longer sends a write again when nobody knows whether the first one applied. retryDecision replaces the old "retry any transport error, retry any 5xx" rule; a write whose answer was lost comes back as client.OutcomeUnknownError, which the CLI maps to exit code 8 and the {"error":…,"code":8,"outcome":"unknown"} envelope. In Canvas Builder the agent is also told while it waits: a change the gateway will hold for the instructor says so before it is sent, and anything else says so once if the answer is slow.
reason:
This is decision D6: the retry fix applies to everyone, not only in Canvas Builder. The generated loop treated every failed HTTP call as transient and every 5xx as worth repeating, so a POST whose answer was lost on the way back was sent up to four times. Canvas applies the first one, the client never sees it, and the course ends up with four copies of the page. Canvas Builder is what brought this to light -- the gateway makes each attempt its own journal entry and its own question for the instructor -- but the fix belongs in the client for every user.

retryDecision is one function with the whole table in its doc comment, rather than the condition spread across the loop, because the interesting part is which cells differ and why. Two cells carry the reasoning: a dial error means nothing was written, so even a create can go again; and PUT and DELETE are idempotent at Canvas, so a resend outside Canvas Builder is harmless, while inside it a resend is a second line in the journal and possibly a second prompt.

A 5xx is an answer, so it is not an unknown outcome -- the server says it failed. It is still not retried for a create, because a 500 from a Rails stack can arrive after the record was written.

The gateway's own 502 outranks the status code. When Canvas Builder says it sent the change on and heard nothing back, nothing the client does will settle it, and its sentence is the one the agent should read. OutcomeUnknownError.Error() is therefore exactly sandbox.MsgUnknownOutcome, with the method, path and cause kept on the struct for a caller that logs rather than prints.

The message is matched against the body as it arrived, before sanitizeJSONResponse rewrites anything credential-shaped, so a sanitizer rule can never turn a refusal into an ordinary 502.

Notices are built once per request rather than per attempt, so a retried POST doesn't repeat itself. The approval notice goes out before the request, because the point of it is to explain the wait that is about to start; the still-waiting notice goes out from a timer and only if the answer hasn't come, because an ordinary page edit should say nothing at all. The two are exclusive: when the change is predicted to be held, the stronger sentence is the only one said.

sandbox.PredictApproval mirrors the gateway's rule 6 (policy.needsApproval) for the cases worth a sentence, and deliberately not for all of them: an upload preflight that would overwrite, a file copy or rename over an existing file, a course update that publishes, and a change to who an item is assigned to are all held by the gateway but fall through to the still-waiting notice here. A guess that comes up short says something weaker; a guess that overreaches would tell the agent a person is being asked when none is.

It reads a body in both shapes the CLI sends: Rails bracket keys ("course[event]"), which go out form-encoded, and nested maps or structs, which go out as JSON. The gateway reads both back to the same parameter, so a prediction that only understood one shape would be silent on half the real calls.

Client.backoff is a field so a test can make the wait nothing. It defaults to cliutil.Backoff, which is what the loop called directly before.
known_limitations:
A context the caller cancelled or whose deadline expired is still returned as the context error, before retryDecision sees it, which is the behaviour every existing caller depends on. In Canvas Builder the approval wait is covered by HTTPClient.Timeout rather than the context (Task 1), so a held approval that outlasts the wait arrives here as a transport timeout and is classified as unknown, which is correct. A caller that sets its own short context deadline on a write would instead get the context error and no unknown-outcome exit code.

PredictApproval is a guess, not the rule. The gateway alone decides what is held, and the cases listed in the reason above are held without a prediction. Nothing downstream may treat a false prediction as "this will not be held".

The still-waiting notice is written once per request. A POST retried after a dial error does not say it again, which is deliberate, but it also means a long second attempt says nothing.

Exit code 9 and the gateway's other refusals are still unmapped: a 403 carrying MsgBlocked is classified as an auth error today. That is Task 4.

The 429 path is unchanged, including its Retry-After handling and the line it prints to stderr rather than to Notices.

The five hunks in internal/client/client.go and the three additions in internal/cli/helpers.go are edits to generated files. A reprint will drop them; this record is what puts them back.
validated_outcome:
go vet ./... clean; go test ./... passing across all eight packages on darwin/arm64 with Go 1.27.1; go test -race ./internal/client/ ./internal/sandbox/ ./internal/cli/ passing.

New coverage. internal/client/retry_test.go, against the fake gateway: a POST the fake drops comes back as OutcomeUnknownError with exactly the unknown-outcome message and exactly one POST at the gateway [Review Focus 2]; a POST answered 500 makes one request and comes back as an APIError, not as unknown; a PUT answered with the gateway's 502 makes one request and reads as the gateway's sentence; a dropped PUT makes one request in Canvas Builder and between two and four outside it; a GET answered 503 twice succeeds on the third request; a transport that fails to dial once then works makes two transport calls and one request at the gateway; a DELETE held 100ms prints the approval notice once and is sent once [Review Focus 1]; a PUT held 200ms with stillWaitingAfter at 50ms prints the still-waiting notice once and never the approval one, while a PUT answered at once prints neither; and a held DELETE outside Canvas Builder prints nothing at all. A 20-row table pins retryDecision itself, cell for cell against the plan's table.

internal/sandbox/approval_test.go has one row per rule in PredictApproval's list, in both body shapes, plus the plan's two negative rows (a page PUT with a real body, a page POST) and a struct body whose blank syllabus_body is still read as held.

internal/cli/outcome_test.go asserts ExitCode is 8, the error text is exactly the unknown-outcome message, the envelope is {"error","code":8,"outcome":"unknown"}, and that a wrapped OutcomeUnknownError is still found.

golangci-lint run --max-issues-per-linter=0 --max-same-issues=0 reports nothing in retry.go, outcome.go, notice.go, approval.go or any of the new tests. The findings in client.go and helpers.go are the pre-existing generated-code ones (import order, unchecked Fprintln); gofmt -d on both shows only the generated import blocks, nothing from these hunks.

CodeRabbit reviewed the patch and raised two findings, both false: that internal/sandbox defines none of ApprovalNotice, StillWaitingNotice, MsgUnknownOutcome, CanvasBuilderMessage or MsgNoJobLabel, and that internal/gatewaytest and the sandboxClient helper do not exist, so neither package could compile. All of them are in HEAD, from Tasks 1 and 2; the review ran with --uncommitted, which shows it only this patch's diff. go build ./... and the full test run are the proof, and were already green before the review.
